domain: Prompt engineering and meta‑optimization for LLM pipelines
pipeline_purpose: Automatically evolve PromptPotter's meta‑prompt templates to accelerate inner‑cycle convergence on the JustLogic depth‑6/7 benchmark (deductive TRUE/FALSE/Uncertain reasoning).
data_characteristics: Textual meta‑prompt templates (six fields per node) for four nodes; fitness signals are numeric deltas and round counts from inner runs with 16 samples per round and up to 2 rounds. Inner origin ~0.44 vs target 0.60 — real headroom, so meta‑prompt edits move the score rather than saturating.
optimization_goals: Maximize first_round_delta and after_N_rounds_delta while minimizing rounds_to_N on JustLogic d6/7. The inner model over‑hedges to 'Uncertain'; the win is meta‑prompt edits that make the inner optimizer break the hedge bias faster (premise‑by‑premise entailment, definitive TRUE/FALSE commitment).
key_challenges: High dimensionality of free‑prose fields causing noise; a small inner panel (16 samples) leading to noisy fitness estimates; balancing categorical vs free‑text slots; ensuring stability of high‑dim slots across rounds; the inner loop's default hedge bias.
upstream_context: Outer optimization loop generates mutation proposals for meta‑prompt fields; inner cycle executes with current meta‑prompts to produce outputs and compute scores.
downstream_context: Composite fitness scores are aggregated to select the best meta‑prompt configurations for the next outer iteration.
raw_description:
# Task: evolve PromptPotter's own meta-prompts

Goal: outer cycle mutates inner cycle's L1 / L1_CRITIQUE / L2 / L3
meta-prompt template fields (6 per node × 4 nodes = 24 fields) so inner
cycles converge faster / further on JustLogic depth-6/7 as proxy benchmark.

## Fitness

Composite formula in ``campaign.json::scoring`` — three proxies:

- ``first_round_delta`` — inner-round-1 score minus inner origin (cheap signal)
- ``after_N_rounds_delta`` — inner-round-N score minus origin (workhorse)
- ``rounds_to_N`` — rounds to hit ``inner_tasks.json::target_score``, capped at ``max_inner_rounds``

Better = higher delta after N AND/OR fewer rounds to target.

## Mutation surface

- Per-node six-field PromptTemplate scheme: ``persona``, ``task_intent``,
  ``problem_description``, ``instruction``, ``thinking_style``, ``answer_format``
- Exposed at ``pipeline.json::nodes.{node}.optimizer.param_keys``
- Four nodes: ``l1_generate``, ``l1_critique``, ``l2_context``, ``l3_plan``.
  Outer L1 may mutate any subset per round
- Out of scope (belongs to inner cycle): inner ``pipeline_params``,
  inner ``optimizer_llm``

## Intuition (don't bake in — algo should rediscover)

- Dimensionality is non-uniform across the 24 fields:
  - bool / categorical slot → doubles state space
  - free-prose slot (``instruction``, ``thinking_style``, ...) →
    explodes it → more signal AND more noise per round
- The inner benchmark (JustLogic d6/7) is a deductive TRUE/FALSE/Uncertain
  task where the inner model over-hedges to 'Uncertain'. The highest-leverage
  meta-edits push the inner optimizer to reward committing to TRUE/FALSE
  under strict entailment and to check premises one by one
- Corollary: L2 / L3 shouldn't read early variance on a high-dim slot
  as "axis unstable, avoid" — that's the slot doing what high-dim
  slots do

## Proxy realism

JustLogic d6/7 (``n_samples_per_inner_round: 16``, ``max_inner_rounds: 2``,
origin ~0.44 < target 0.60) keeps each outer "sample" at order-of-minutes
rather than -hours while leaving real headroom for the meta-prompt edits to
move the inner score. Trade-off is signal quality — bump sample count before
publication runs. See ``docs/specs/l4-outer-loop.md`` § Finish line.
